learningObjective: Diagnose why a measured GEMM throughput falls significantly below the theoretical peak and identify the most plausible cause.
profileData: cuBLAS FP16 GEMM (M=N=K=8192): measured throughput 220 TFLOP/s; theoretical peak 312 TFLOP/s (dense FP16 Tensor Core, A100 SXM). Nsight Compute reports 78% Tensor Core utilization and no HBM saturation.
stem: You measure 220 TFLOP/s on a cuBLAS FP16 GEMM (M=N=K=8192) on an A100 SXM, versus a theoretical peak of 312 TFLOP/s. Nsight Compute shows 78% Tensor Core utilization and HBM is not saturated. Which explanation is most consistent with the data?

options.text: cuBLAS is memory-bound on this size, so achieved throughput is HBM × AI; the ridge point is above the achieved value.

Tensor Cores are not fully occupied every cycle (78% Tensor Core utilization); typical causes include tile boundary effects, epilogue/prologue, imperfect scheduling, and warp scheduler stalls, producing the gap from the 312 TFLOP/s ceiling.
Kernel launch overhead dominates; the 30% gap is CPU-side launch overhead not overlapping with compute.
The A100 SXM ridge point is 78 FLOP/byte and this GEMM sits exactly on the ridge, so the measured value equals the ceiling.

explanation: For M=N=K=8192 FP16, AI ≈ 8192/3 ≈ 2731 FLOP/byte, well above A100's FP16 ridge (~156 FLOP/byte), so the kernel is deeply compute-bound and HBM is not the bottleneck (consistent with the profile). The measured 220 TFLOP/s ≈ 78% × 312 TFLOP/s matches the reported Tensor Core utilization. Typical gaps come from prologue/epilogue, tile-boundary padding, warp-scheduler stalls and non-ideal MMA pipeline packing. Options A (memory-bound), C (launch overhead), and D (ridge alignment) contradict the profile or the AI.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: HBM is not saturated and AI is far above ridge; kernel is compute-bound.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: 78% Tensor Core utilization × 312 TFLOP/s ≈ 244 TFLOP/s (order-of-magnitude match with 220), and the classical causes of the gap fit the profile.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: launch overhead is microseconds; a single GEMM of this size runs many milliseconds. Launch overhead cannot explain a 30% shortfall.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: A100 FP16 ridge is ~156 FLOP/byte and the GEMM AI is ~2731 FLOP/byte; the operation is far above the ridge.

assumptions: Single-kernel steady-state GEMM measurement; not a batch-of-tiny-kernels regime.
cuBLAS handle, FP16 inputs and outputs, no exotic epilogue fusion.
nonImplications: Does not imply Tensor Core utilization percentage directly maps to achieved TFLOP/s at any ratio; the mapping is approximate and depends on how the metric is defined by Nsight Compute.
Does not imply moving to a larger K would necessarily hit peak; other factors (SM occupancy, MMA scheduling) still cap it.

distractorRationales.A: Ignores profile evidence (HBM not saturated) and AI computation.
distractorRationales.C: Wrong order of magnitude for launch overhead scope.

sourceRefs.locator: Tensor Core utilization / SM active metrics; interpretation guide

performanceClaim.scope: A100 SXM, cuBLAS FP16 GEMM 8192×8192×8192, diagnosis of ~70% of peak
